dedupe_keys.name: end to end handover simulator for 5g heterogeneous networks

description: This simulator evaluates handover algorithms in 5G heterogeneous networks of macro and small cells, developed at the Universidade de Vigo by José Manuel Rúa-Estévez, Pablo Fondo-Ferreiro, Felipe Gil-Castiñeira and Francisco Javier González-Castaño and published with an article in the IEEE Open Journal of the Communications Society. It has two parts: a C++ network simulator built on ns-3 and its 5G-LENA module, which generates radio traces and performance metrics for a scenario, and a Python handover simulator that replays those traces to test arbitrary handover algorithms, with four implemented, including the 3GPP Release 15 algorithm. Coverage: configurable synthetic scenarios. Format and access: source code with scenario files on Zenodo, free under the MIT licence. Caveats: research code; large ns-3 runs are needed to produce traces; scenarios are synthetic. Simulation uses: capacity planning of dense 5G deployments and evaluation of mobility management, including service continuity when cells fail. Related records: it runs on the ns-3 platform with the 5G-LENA module, and NordicDat gives measured handover conditions.
